the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Fix r, r' in R. The local dimension dim_r(R) is independent of the point: the homogeneous lemma gives a field extension k'/k and an isomorphism of the s-fibres over Spec(k') carrying a point over r to a point over r'; by Morphisms, dimension-fibre-after-base-change the fibre dimension is unchanged by the base change, so dim_r(R) = dim_{r'}(R); call the common value d. By Morphisms, dimension-fibre-at-a-point applied with s and with t, dim_r(R) = dim(O_{R,r}) + trdeg_{s(k)}(kappa(r)) = dim(O_{R,r}) + trdeg_{t(k)}(kappa(r)); since both s and t identify k inside kappa(r) the two transcendence degrees both equal trdeg_k(kappa(r)), whence they are equal. Finally, by Properties, codimension-local-ring the dimension of R, and of any open subset of R, is the supremum of the dimensions of the local rings; this supremum is maximal at a closed point r, and for a closed point trdeg_k(kappa(r)) = 0 by the Hilbert Nullstellensatz (Morphisms, Section points-finite-type). Hence d = dim(O_{R,r}) at closed points and dim(R) = d, which gives all four assertions: R is equidimensional, dim(R) = dim_r(R) for every r, the two transcendence degrees agree for every r, and dim(R) = dim(O_{R,r}) for every closed point r.
